title: NIH SBIR/STTR (Parent SBIR PA-27-100 [R43/R44]; Parent STTR PA-27-102 [R41/R42])
funder: National Institutes of Health (with CDC and FDA) - NIH SEED Office
deadline_note: Next standard due date: January 5, 2027, 5:00 PM local time of the applicant organization. The one after is April 5, 2027; the current parent announcements PA-27-100 and PA-27-102 expire April 6, 2027. NIH's standard small-business due dates are September 5, January 5 and April 5 each year. No late applications are accepted for this NOFO.
amount: Phase I: normally up to $335,937 total costs (SBA guideline per NIH SEED); several NIH institutes allow up to $400,000 or $700,000. Phase II: $2,239,578 guideline (up to $2.5M-$3M at some institutes). Non-dilutive grant.

summary.at_a_glance: NIH's Seed Fund gives non-dilutive R&D grants to U.S. small businesses developing health and life-science products. Most companies apply to the 'parent' announcements (SBIR PA-27-100, STTR PA-27-102) at one of three standard due dates a year. Legislative authority for the programs expired on October 1, 2025 (NIH expired all its small-business announcements) and was restored on April 13, 2026 through September 30, 2031; new announcements were posted May 28, 2026 and applications are being accepted again.
summary.what_they_offer: Phase I grant to establish technical merit and feasibility; Phase II to continue R&D toward commercialization. Total funding (direct costs, indirect costs and fee) normally may not exceed SBA budget guidelines: NIH SEED lists $335,937 for Phase I and $2,239,578 for Phase II. PA-27-100 lists higher institute-specific guidelines, e.g. Phase I $700,000 at NCI, NIA, NIAID, NIGMS, NIMH, NINDS and NCCIH and $400,000 at NHLBI, NEI, NHGRI, NIAAA, NICHD, NIDCD, NIDDK, NIDA and NINR; other components follow the SBA guideline. The NOFO says award periods normally may not exceed 6 months for Phase I and 2 years for Phase II (the NIH SEED site describes Phase I timelines of 6 months to 2 years). A fee of up to 7% of total costs may be requested. Fast-Track (Phase I and II together) and Direct to Phase II are NIH-only options. Technical and Business Assistance of up to $6,500 per Phase I project is available.
summary.what_theyre_looking_for: Reviewers give an overall impact score and score five criteria: Significance (important problem or unmet need; for Phase I, commercial potential to lead to a marketable product or service), Investigator(s), Innovation (innovative solution with meaningful competitive advantages over existing approaches), Approach (for Phase I: will the strategy establish feasibility, are risky aspects managed, and are there clear, appropriate, measurable milestones before Phase II) and Environment (scientific and business environment; appropriate business expertise and resources). The project must fit the mission of a participating NIH, CDC or FDA component.
summary.who_can_apply: Only United States small business concerns: organized for profit with a place of business in the United States, not more than 500 employees including affiliates, and more than 50% directly owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (or by multiple venture capital, hedge fund or private equity firms, which requires an extra certification). An LLC is an accepted legal form. For SBIR the PD/PI's primary employment must be with the small business at the time of award and during the project. In SBIR Phase I normally two-thirds (67%) of the research effort is carried out by the small business. Foreign organizations are not eligible, and applications involving foreign subawards are not accepted. HHS accepts at most nine new and resubmission Phase I, Fast-Track and Direct to Phase II applications or proposals from one small business per fiscal year.
summary.how_to_apply: 1) Complete the registrations (can take 6 weeks or more): SAM.gov with Unique Entity Identifier, SBA Company Registry (gives the SBC Control ID), eRA Commons (a Signing Official account and a separate PD/PI account, PD/PI linked to an ORCID iD) and Grants.gov. 2) Optional but encouraged: talk to an NIH program officer at the institute that fits the project. 3) Prepare the SF424 (R&R) application package in NIH ASSIST (or Grants.gov Workspace) following the SBIR/STTR (B) Instructions, Forms Version I. 4) The Signing Official submits by 5:00 PM local time on the due date; track and view the assembled application in eRA Commons. 5) Peer review (scientific merit review roughly 2-3 months after the due date), then advisory council review and an award decision; for the January 5, 2027 date the NOFO lists review in March 2027, council in May 2027 and earliest start July 2027.
summary.worth_noting: A Commercialization Plan is NOT allowed in a Phase I SBIR application, and Phase I appendix materials are not permitted. A Data Management and Sharing Plan is not applicable for this NOFO. The current forms version is still Forms Version I (for due dates on or after January 25, 2025); the SBIR/STTR instructions were last re-released in December 2025, which introduced the Biographical Sketch Common Form and NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement prepared in SciENcv. Applicants under consideration must later file the SBA foreign-affiliations disclosure form; NIH cannot fund a company with certain ties to foreign countries of concern. Clinical trials are optional under the parent NOFO but not every institute accepts them. Choose STTR (PA-27-102) instead if the project depends on a formal collaboration with a nonprofit research institution.

portal.platform: NIH ASSIST (eRA) or Grants.gov Workspace; status tracked in eRA Commons
portal.notes: There is no simple web form: the application is a multi-form federal package (SF424 (R&R)) with many PDF attachments, prepared in ASSIST by people with eRA Commons accounts and submitted by the organization's Signing Official. Registration in SAM.gov, the SBA Company Registry, eRA Commons and Grants.gov must be finished first and can take 6 weeks or more; an eRA Commons account alone can take up to 2 weeks. If the PD/PI is also the Signing Official they need two distinct eRA Commons accounts. Biographical sketches must be digitally certified PDFs produced in SciENcv. NIH validates page limits and other rules on submission, so submit early to fix errors before the deadline. The portals were not opened for this check (login required); CAPTCHA not observed.

questions_note: NIH has no question-style form; the list is the set of required forms, attachments and form fields for a new Phase I SBIR application, taken on 2026-11-24 from the official 'SBIR/STTR Instructions for NIH and Other PHS Agencies - Forms Version I Series' (PDF dated December 2025, 177 pages), NIH's Table of Page Limits (last updated September 30, 2026) and the parent announcement PA-27-100. Item names and help text are verbatim from those documents (help text is excerpted, not the complete instruction). Page limits: Specific Aims 1 page, Research Strategy 6 pages for Phase I (R43/R41), Introduction 1 page (resubmissions only), Commercialization Plan 12 pages (Phase II/Fast-Track only); Project Summary/Abstract is limited to 30 lines of text and Project Narrative to three sentences (these two limits are stated in help because they are not page, word or character limits). The Regulatory Plan (2-page maximum) applies only to clinical-trial applications. The three Research Strategy headings are listed as separate entries although they are uploaded as one PDF. Not itemized: the individual fields of the SF 424 cover form, budget form, performance-site form and the Human Subjects study record; see the guide for those. The ASSIST screens themselves were not viewed (login required).

questions.help: The cover letter is for internal use only and will not be shared with peer reviewers. Refer to the “content” list below for items that are permitted, as well as for specific situations in which a cover letter must be included.

questions.section: R&R Other Project Information Form - attachments
questions.help: The "Project Summary/Abstract" attachment is required. This section is limited to 30 lines of text, and must follow the required font and margin specifications. State the application's broad, long-term objectives and specific aims, making reference to the health relatedness of the project (i.e., relevance to the mission of the agency). Describe the research design and methods for achieving the stated goals. Do not include proprietary, confidential information or trade secrets in the project summary.

questions.section: R&R Other Project Information Form - attachments
questions.help: The "Project Narrative" attachment is required. Describe the relevance of this research to public health in, at most, three sentences.

questions.section: R&R Other Project Information Form - attachments
questions.help: The “Bibliography & References Cited” attachment is required unless otherwise noted in the NOFO. The “Bibliography & References Cited” attachment should include any references cited in B.400 - PHS 398 Research Plan Form and in the B.500 - PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information form. While there is not a page limitation, it is important to be concise and to select only those literature references pertinent to the proposed research.

questions.section: R&R Other Project Information Form - attachments
questions.help: The “Facilities & Other Resources” attachment is required unless otherwise specified in the NOFO. Describe how the scientific environment in which the research will be done contributes to the probability of success (e.g., institutional support, physical resources, and intellectual rapport). Effective for applications submitted for due dates on or after September 5, 2023, in addition to describing the scientific environment and the company support, the applicant must describe the business environment and resources, or how the company will obtain access to the appropriate business resources, for completing and commercializing the proposed product or service. This includes any relevant intellectual property associated with the project necessary to facilitate commercialization.

questions.section: R&R Other Project Information Form - attachments
questions.help: The “Equipment” attachment is required. List major items of equipment already available for this project and, if appropriate, identify the equipment's location and pertinent capabilities.

questions.section: R&R Other Project Information Form - attachments
questions.help: Attach a file to provide additional information only in accordance with the NOFO and/or agency-specific instructions. If applicable, attach a “Foreign Justification” here. Applications that propose a clinical trial must include the Regulatory Plan attachment. Applications that DO NOT propose a clinical trial must NOT submit the Regulatory Plan attachment.

questions.section: R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) Form - attachments
questions.help: The Biographical Sketch Common Form and NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement are required by each individual identified as a senior/key person on a Federally funded research project. Applicants are required to use Science Experts Network Curriculum Vitae (SciENcv) to complete the Biographical Sketch Common Form and the NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement to produce digitally certified PDF(s) for use in application submission.

The “Budget Justification” attachment is required. Attach only one file. Use the Budget Justification to provide the additional information requested in each budget category identified above and any other information the applicant wishes to submit to support the budget request.

questions.text: 1. Introduction to Application (for Resubmission and Revision applications)
questions.help: An "Introduction to Application" attachment is required only if the type of application is resubmission or revision or if the NOFO specifies that one is needed. An introduction is not allowed for new or renewal applications.

The “Specific Aims” attachment is required unless otherwise specified in the NOFO. State concisely the goals of the proposed research and summarize the expected outcome(s), including the impact that the results of the proposed research will have on the research field(s) involved. Phase I Applications: State the specific objectives of the Phase I research and development effort, including the technical questions you will try to answer to determine the Phase I feasibility of the proposed approach and the impact of the proposed research and development. State concisely and realistically what the proposed R&D is intended to accomplish in terms of its potential for technological innovation and commercial application. Define the proposed process or service to ultimately be developed. Include clear and measurable milestones for each of the aims as these will be used in the evaluation process.

The “Research Strategy” attachment is required. Organize the Research Strategy in the specified order and use the instructions provided below unless otherwise specified in the NOFO. Start each section with the appropriate heading – Significance, Innovation, Approach. Although multiple sections of information are required in the Research Strategy as detailed below, the page limit applies to the entirety of the single "Research Strategy" attachment.

- Explain the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress that the proposed project addresses.
- Describe the strengths and weaknesses in the rigor of the prior research (both published and unpublished) that serves as the key support for the proposed project.
- Explain how the proposed project will improve scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice in one or more broad fields.
- Explain the project’s potential to lead to a marketable product, process, or service.

- Explain how the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms.
- Describe any novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation or interventions to be developed or used, and any advantage over existing methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions.
- Explain any refinements, improvements, or new applications of theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions.

- Describe the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses to be used to accomplish the specific aims of the project.
- Discuss potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success anticipated to achieve the aims.
- If the project is in the early stages of development, describe any strategy to establish feasibility, and address the management of any high risk aspects of the proposed work.
- Provide a tentative sequence or timetable for the project.
- Phase I Applications: Preliminary data are not required for Phase I Applications; however, such results may assist reviewers in assessing the likelihood of success of the proposed project and may be included in the Research Strategy attachment.
A “Progress Report Publication List” attachment is required only if the type of application is renewal.
Include a “Vertebrate Animals” attachment if you answered “Yes” to the question “Are Vertebrate Animals Used?” on the B.220 - R&R Other Project Information Form.

Include a “Select Agent Research” attachment if your proposed activities involve the use of select agents at any time during the proposed project period, either at the applicant organization or at any performance site.
Any applicant who designates multiple PD/PIs (on the B.240 - R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) Form) must include a Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan.
Include a “Consortium/Contractual Arrangements” attachment if you have consortiums/contracts in your budget.

Combine all letters of support into a single PDF file and attach this information here. Involvement of consultants and collaborators in the planning and research stages of the project is permitted. With the application, letters are required from each individual and / or collaborator confirming their role(s) in the project. The letter(s) should be prepared on the consultant or collaborator’s letterhead and addressed to the small business. One page is recommended. Letters of interest from potential commercial partners or investors and letters of commitment of funds or other resources that will enhance the likelihood of commercialization should be placed following the letters of support for consultants and collaborators.

Sharing Model Organisms: Regardless of the amount requested, all applications where the development of model organisms is anticipated are expected to include a description of a specific plan for sharing and distributing unique model organisms or state why such sharing is restricted or not possible.
A Data Management and Sharing Plan is not applicable for this NOFO.
